Hi all — ops notes and feasibility:

- Onshore-only processing: feasible. We can route CareLoom traffic to our US-dedicated pool (region: us-east-1 / us-west-2) and apply network ACLs to limit egress. That lane will have separate instance pools and a tenant tag for auditability.

- Retention windows: we support three practical tiers out of the box: 0 days (ephemeral, session-only KV cache that evicts immediately after session termination), 7 days (accident recovery), and 30 days (default). The 0-day option requires ephemeral session tokens only and a short TTL on any persisted logs.

- KMS options: 1) Redwood-managed onshore KMS, 2) Customer-managed KMS (BYOK) with HSM-backed keys and per-tenant key policies. BYOK adds ~3-4 weeks to onboarding due to key exchange and HSM configuration.

- Audit / proof-of-deletion: we can provide an append-only deletion log (hashes + timestamp) and a runbook describing deletion order and verification steps. For customers requiring attestation, we can produce a compliance statement signed by Redwood security after deletion events.

Attachments: no-train-ops-runbook-stub.txt

Let me know which retention tier and KMS option you prefer so we can finalize the amendment.

-David
